content.title: A house full of thread
content.text: Paris, Christmas Day 1911. A girl is born into a family that lives among old tapestries. Her parents buy them, repair them and sell them.

content.title: The workshop
content.text: Below the family’s home is a workshop where worn tapestries are mended. When part of a design has faded away, the girl draws it back in.

content.title: Her mother’s needle
content.text: Her mother runs the workshop. She is patient and precise, and she repairs what is torn instead of throwing it away. The girl never forgets that.

content.title: What nobody says
content.text: An English tutor comes to live with the family. For ten years everyone knows what nobody says: the father is in love with her. The girl keeps quiet, and remembers everything.

content.title: Rules that never change
content.text: Looking for order, she studies mathematics at the Sorbonne. Geometry feels safe: its rules never change.
Her mother dies while she is still a student. She leaves mathematics behind and turns to art. From now on, she wants to make things with her hands.

content.title: A new city
content.text: Louise marries an American art historian, and in 1938 they settle in New York. She takes her past with her, and keeps almost everything.

content.title: Late, but not too late
content.text: For decades she makes art that few people notice. She keeps going. In 1982, at seventy, the Museum of Modern Art in New York gives her a first retrospective.

content.title: Mother spider
content.text: Her best-known animal is a spider, many metres tall. For Louise it stands for her mother: a weaver who repairs, protects and is patient.

content.title: The cupboard
content.text: Late in life she opens her cupboards: nightgowns, scarves, table napkins and hand towels from her wedding trousseau, some kept since the 1920s. Then she starts to cut them up.

content.title: A book without paper
content.text: From that cloth she sews a book. Every page is fabric: stripes, checks, circles and grids, pieced together with needle and thread.

content.title: The last page
content.text: She once wrote: “I had a flashback of something that never existed.” Her book is closer than you think. You have been carrying its pieces.

fragments.title: Blue dots
fragments.caption: Earned at Sint-Carolus Borromeuskerk.
fragments.off: Dots in a perfect grid. Look at the wall: no dots like these. We made it.

fragments.title: Green ladder
fragments.caption: Earned at Plantin-Moretus.
fragments.off: A ladder of stripes that climbs nowhere. It’s not on her wall – it’s ours.

fragments.title: Red crosshatch
fragments.caption: Earned at MoMu.
fragments.off: A crosshatch, drawn line by line. You won’t find it on her pages. We made it.

fragments.title: Pink half-moons
fragments.caption: Earned at Bourla.
fragments.off: Half-moons in a neat row. Pretty, but not hers – we made it.

fragments.title: Navy waves
fragments.caption: Earned at Maagdenhuis.
fragments.off: Navy waves. Look at the wall again: there are no waves. We made it.

fragments.title: Black zigzag
fragments.caption: Hidden in the KMSKA.
fragments.off: A zigzag to fool you. It’s on none of her pages on the wall.

_fragments_note: Fragments are pages of Ode à l'oubli. "real": true = a page of the real work, cut from scripts/fragments/ode-a-loubli-photo.png; the fakes are our own cloth pages in the same style (scripts/fragments/make-fakes.py). A sharper photo gives sharper pieces (see README). "off" (fakes only): what gave the fake away, shown in the finale.
_hooks_note: Hooks hang anywhere in the streets (no fixed spot, the coordinates are only used by the dev panel). The diary chapters come in the order you find hooks: your 1st hook = chapter 1, your 2nd = chapter 2, … whatever QR it is. Chapters tell Louise Bourgeois' story without giving away the artwork before the KMSKA. Sources: MoMA collection (Ode à l'oubli), Wikipedia.

finale.alt: Ode à l'oubli: 36 framed fabric pages on a museum wall.
finale.title: Louise Bourgeois
finale.subtitle: Ode à l’oubli (Ode to forgetting), 2002
finale.text: A book without paper. Every page is sewn from cloth she kept for most of her life: nightgowns, scarves, table napkins and hand towels from her wedding trousseau. The girl who grew up in a tapestry workshop mended her memories with needle and thread.
finale.closing: She repaired what was torn. Today, piece by piece, so did you.
finale._photo: From the photo the team shared (scripts/fragments/ode-a-loubli-photo.png). "place" of each real fragment is in this picture's pixels (size).

cards.title: Louise Bourgeois.
cards.text: Born in Paris in 1911, she grew up in her parents’ tapestry workshop. She became one of the great artists of the 20th century, and kept making art until she died in 2010, at 98.

cards.title: Ode à l’oubli.
cards.text: 2002. A book without paper: 36 pages, sewn from cloth instead. The pages hang on the wall in front of you – your pieces are cut from them.

cards.title: the cloth was hers.
cards.text: Nightgowns, scarves, napkins and hand towels from her wedding trousseau, kept for most of her life. For the girl from the tapestry workshop, sewing meant repairing. Mending the cloth was mending her memories.
